name: More Adey
bio: Translator and editor who published the first English translation of Ibsen's Brand (1891) under the pseudonym William Wilson, later ran the Carfax picture gallery with Robert Ross, and was joint editor of the Burlington Magazine, 1911-19. The editors of the Complete Letters describe him as a 'Close friend of Robert Ross'; the two shared lodgings at 24 Hornton Street, Kensington, and both were Roman Catholics - Wilde in 1897 teased 'you and More, especially More' as a unit for treating him 'as a Dissenter'. It was to Adey that Ross addressed, in installments, his narrative of Wilde's final illness, death and funeral (14 December 1900), and a rosary Adey had given Ross was placed around Wilde's neck at the laying-out.
bio_note: Born/died, Brand translation, 'Close friend of Robert Ross' and Carfax partnership from the biographical footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 577 n. 2 (repo PDF 629; Burlington Magazine editorship also in the elided portion of that note, which cites Siegfried Sassoon, Siegfried's Journey, 1945, for his later years). Shared lodgings from the editorial note at p. 781 n. 2 (PDF 832): 'More Adey and Robert Ross shared lodgings at 24 Hornton Street, Kensington'. 'You and More' and the editors' 'Ross and Adey were both Roman Catholics' from p. 866 and n. 1 (PDF 916). Death-narrative addressee and rosary from the Epilogue, pp. 1219 and 1221 (PDF 1264, 1266). All pages read as page images 2026-08-03; printed folios confirmed. Full passages in dossiers/ADEY-GILBERT-TURNER_dossier.md. No source read asserts a romantic or sexual dimension to the Ross household partnership; see the dossier's null-finding note.
